"4c85940e-5d6a-5e77-8c03-607d21fd581c"] [:db/add "4c85940e-5d6a-5e77-8c03-607d21fd581c" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \frac{y^{2} - 1}{y^{2}}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "4c85940e-5d6a-5e77-8c03-607d21fd581c" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y\ne0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} - 1}{c^{2}}
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=1$ and $y=-1$."] [:db/add "4c85940e-5d6a-5e77-8c03-607d21fd581c" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "4c85940e-5d6a-5e77-8c03-607d21fd581c" :question/answer-fields #uuid "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e"] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y^{2} - 3 y - 2
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = - c^{2} - 3 c - 2
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=-3 - 2 - 1 \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=-2 - 1 + 3 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-4 - 2 + 6 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-1$ and $y=-2$."] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/answer-fields Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ - c - \sin{\left(c \right)} - \pi\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=0$: Use $\sin{\left(0 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=- \pi + 0 - \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=- \pi$: Use $\sin{\left(- \pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(- \pi)= \\ - \pi - \sin{\left(- \pi \right)} + \pi \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=\pi$: Use $\sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(\pi)= \\ - \pi - \pi - \sin{\left(\pi \right)} \\ =- 2 \pi\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f"] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ y^{2} \ln{\left(y \right)} - e^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ c^{2} \ln{\left(c \right)} - e^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(e)= \\ - e^{2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- e^{2} + 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=- e^{2} + 1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=- e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e$."] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/answer-fields $$
f(c) = - c^{2} + c + 2
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=-4 + 2 + 2 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0 + 0 + 2 \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-4 - 2 + 2 \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45"] [:db/add "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{1}{\left(y + 1\right)^{2}}= \\ 1\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1\ne0$.

Rearranging once, test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ 1 - \frac{1}{\left(c + 1\right)^{2}}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- \frac{1}{9} + 1 \\ &=\frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-1 + 1 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=- \frac{1}{4} + 1 \\ &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-2$."] [:db/add "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45" :question/answer-fields #uuid "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745"] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \left(y + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(y + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(c + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1 + e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1 + e) &=e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ &=e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$."] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/answer-fields #uuid "4db980ed-67fb-5185-9224-78c8f7859f26"] [:db/add "4db980ed-67fb-5185-9224-78c8f7859f26" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
f(c) = c^{3} - c^{2} + 2
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=-4 + 2 + 8 \\ &=6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=-1 - 1 + 2 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0 + 0 + 2 \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "d2788ace-5247-5c8a-b2be-3ee65d5917cb"] [:db/add "d2788ace-5247-5c8a-b2be-3ee65d5917cb" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \frac{y^{2} - 5 y + 6}{y - 1}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "d2788ace-5247-5c8a-b2be-3ee65d5917cb" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y - 1\ne0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} - 5 c + 6}{c - 1}
$$

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=- \frac{15}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$, $c - 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=2$ and $y=3$."] [:db/add "d2788ace-5247-5c8a-b2be-3ee65d5917cb" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "d2788ace-5247-5c8a-b2be-3ee65d5917cb" :question/answer-fields #uuid "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880"] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \left(- y - e - 1\right) \ln{\left(- y - 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $- y - 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(- c - e - 1\right) \ln{\left(- c - 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-3)= \\ \left(- e + 2\right) \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-4$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-4)= \\ \left(- e + 3\right) \ln{\left(3 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-2)= \\ \left(- e + 1\right) \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$, $- c - 1=-1$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-2$."] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/answer-fields #uuid "9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a"] [:db/add "9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \left(y - e + 1\right) \ln{\left(y + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(c - e + 1\right) \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(1)= \\ \left(- e + 2\right) \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(0)= \\ \left(- e + 1\right) \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(2)= \\ \left(- e + 3\right) \ln{\left(3 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$, $c + 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$."] [:db/add "9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/answer-fields #uuid "d3cee2a6-f129-5d27-af14-edfba3e17138"] [:db/add "d3cee2a6-f129-5d27-af14-edfba3e17138" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \frac{y^{2} + y - 2}{y - 1}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "d3cee2a6-f129-5d27-af14-edfba3e17138" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y - 1\ne0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} + c - 2}{c - 1}
$$

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$, $c - 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) &=6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-2$."] [:db/add "d3cee2a6-f129-5d27-af14-edfba3e17138" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "d3cee2a6-f129-5d27-af14-edfba3e17138" :question/answer-fields $$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \frac{y^{3} - y^{2} - 6 y}{y - 3}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y - 3\ne0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \frac{c^{3} - c^{2} - 6 c}{c - 3}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=3\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=3$, $c - 3=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$ and $y=-2$."] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "83a60b17-c8d9-5ae3-8b29-42dfd3061910"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "906052da-d6f9-5bc8-b602-f5263b40a0a6"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "880539eb-c7c3-5d4a-958b-a3f8407f4262"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "6ccad5b0-78a1-56f1-adfd-b79a8730cc49"] [:db/ensure "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/questions "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0"] [:db/add "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "ac3f4ddf-e1ea-578a-85d0-b59d3a1b9f79"] [:db/add "generator" :question-generator/script "generators/4f/4fd06a5b0cf48eeed6d10418e1b6cad209e39ef6a90fedc95a4468179725ac42/generator.py"] [:db/add 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] [:db/ensure 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/validate] [:db/cas 17592186693815 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186693821 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186693830 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694166 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694194 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694197 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694208 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694216 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694227 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694244 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694256 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694258 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694284 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694294 :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

The original equation requires $y - 1>0$.

Isolating the derivative gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = y^{2} \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} - 2 y \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}.
$$

Test each supplied constant in the original equation, with the derivative set to zero.

- For $y=c=2$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\  &= 0 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= 3 \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-2} + 3\end{aligned}
$$

The values differ, so this is *not* an equilibrium solution.

- For $y=c=1 + e$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(e \right)} \\  &= 1 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= 2 + e \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-2} + 2 + e + e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The values differ, so this is *not* an equilibrium solution.

- For $y=c=e^{-1} + 1$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)} \\  &= -1 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= e^{-1} + 2 \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-1} + 2\end{aligned}
$$

The values agree, so this is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e^{-1} + 1$." "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

$$

- For $c=1 + e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(1 + e)= \\ e^{-2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ =e^{-2} + e^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} + e^{-2} \\ &=e^{-2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=e^{-1} + 1$: Use $\ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)}=-1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(e^{-1} + 1)= \\ \frac{\ln{\left(e^{-1} \right)}}{e^{2}} + e^{-2} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e^{-1} + 1$."] [:db/ensure 17592186694294 :question/validate]]

#uuid "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e"] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y^{2} - 3 y - 2
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = - c^{2} - 3 c - 2
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=-3 - 2 - 1 \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1) &=-2 - 1 + 3 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-4 - 2 + 6 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-1$ and $y=-2$."] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "368851c4-156d-54b1-afce-4750f12eec6e" :question/answer-fields #uuid "a43b5bf3-6df3-53c4-be0b-ae5caac9b00d"] [:db/add "a43b5bf3-6df3-53c4-be0b-ae5caac9b00d" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ - y - \sin{\left(y \right)} - \pi\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "a43b5bf3-6df3-53c4-be0b-ae5caac9b00d" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ - c - \sin{\left(c \right)} - \pi\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=0$: Use $\sin{\left(0 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=- \pi + 0 - \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=- \pi\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=- \pi$: Use $\sin{\left(- \pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(- \pi)= \\ - \pi - \sin{\left(- \pi \right)} + \pi \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=\pi$: Use $\sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(\pi)= \\ - \pi - \pi - \sin{\left(\pi \right)} \\ =- 2 \pi\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=- \pi$."] [:db/add "a43b5bf3-6df3-53c4-be0b-ae5caac9b00d" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "a43b5bf3-6df3-53c4-be0b-ae5caac9b00d" :question/answer-fields #uuid "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f"] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ y^{2} \ln{\left(y \right)} - e^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ c^{2} \ln{\left(c \right)} - e^{2}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(e)= \\ - e^{2} + e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- e^{2} + 4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=- e^{2} + 1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=- e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=e$."] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "c72d8feb-f5dd-59f4-b471-e2054392ae9f" :question/answer-fields #uuid "25ff952b-9e47-5f63-8fd0-219680477b42"] [:db/add "25ff952b-9e47-5f63-8fd0-219680477b42" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = - y^{2} + y + 2
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "25ff952b-9e47-5f63-8fd0-219680477b42" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = - c^{2} + c + 2
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=-4 + 2 + 2 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0 + 0 + 2 \\ &=2\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-4 - 2 + 2 \\ &=-4\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=2$."] [:db/add "25ff952b-9e47-5f63-8fd0-219680477b42" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "25ff952b-9e47-5f63-8fd0-219680477b42" :question/answer-fields #uuid "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45"] [:db/add "2290f49d-c263-51d2-8038-81eb1905aa45" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt} + \frac{1}{\left(y + 1\right)^{2}}= \\ 1\end{gathered}
$$

Rearranging once, test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ 1 - \frac{1}{\left(c + 1\right)^{2}}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=- \frac{1}{9} + 1 \\ &=\frac{8}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-1 + 1 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=- \frac{1}{4} + 1 \\ &=\frac{3}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745"] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \left(y + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(y + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(c + 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=4 \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1 + e$: Use $\ln{\left(e \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-1 + e) &=e^{2} \ln{\left(e \right)} \\ &=e^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=1 \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$."] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/moderate] [:db/add "141a55c9-d09e-52ce-941e-f884a7716745" :question/answer-fields #uuid "86972ed0-fdb5-5c6a-a3da-dc7cbd5ab885"] [:db/add "86972ed0-fdb5-5c6a-a3da-dc7cbd5ab885" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ 2 \sin{\left(y - 1 \right)}\end{gathered}

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "86972ed0-fdb5-5c6a-a3da-dc7cbd5ab885" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = 2 \sin{\left(c - 1 \right)}
$$

- For $c=- \frac{\pi}{2} + 1$: Use $\sin{\left(- \frac{\pi}{2} \right)}=-1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(- \frac{\pi}{2} + 1)= \\ 2 \sin{\left(- \frac{\pi}{2} \right)} \\ =-2\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$: Use $\sin{\left(0 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=2 \sin{\left(0 \right)} \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1 + \frac{\pi}{2}$: Use $\sin{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \right)}=1$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(1 + \frac{\pi}{2})= \\ 2 \sin{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \right)} \\ =2\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "4db980ed-67fb-5185-9224-78c8f7859f26"] [:db/add "4db980ed-67fb-5185-9224-78c8f7859f26" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} -2 = y^{3} - y^{2}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "4db980ed-67fb-5185-9224-78c8f7859f26" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

Rearranging once, test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = c^{3} - c^{2} + 2
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=-4 + 2 + 8 \\ &=6\end{aligned}
$$

Rearranging once, test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = - 2 c^{2} - 4 c
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=-8 + 8 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=-4 - 2 \\ &=-6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0 + 0 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$, $c - 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880"] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \left(- y - e - 1\right) \ln{\left(- y - 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $- y - 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(- c - e - 1\right) \ln{\left(- c - 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-3)= \\ \left(- e + 2\right) \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-4$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-4)= \\ \left(- e + 3\right) \ln{\left(3 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(-2)= \\ \left(- e + 1\right) \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$, $- c - 1=-1$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=-2$."] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "4c6e3e44-5152-5185-b121-d74f84d2d880" :question/answer-fields $$

$$
\begin{gathered}f(0)= \\ \left(- e + 1\right) \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(2)= \\ \left(- e + 3\right) \ln{\left(3 \right)}\end{gathered}

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$, $c + 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} + c - 2}{c - 1}
$$

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$, $c - 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) &=6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

#uuid "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{dy}{dt}= \\ \frac{y^{3} - y^{2} - 6 y}{y - 3}\end{gathered}
$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/worked-solution "An equilibrium is a constant function $y(t)=c$. Set $dy/dt=0$ and test the resulting equation.

First keep the original domain: $y - 3\ne0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \frac{c^{3} - c^{2} - 6 c}{c - 3}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=3\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=3$, $c - 3=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$ and $y=-2$."] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "83a60b17-c8d9-5ae3-8b29-42dfd3061910"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "906052da-d6f9-5bc8-b602-f5263b40a0a6"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "880539eb-c7c3-5d4a-958b-a3f8407f4262"] [:db/add "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/answer-fields "6ccad5b0-78a1-56f1-adfd-b79a8730cc49"] [:db/ensure "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0" :question/validate] [:db/add 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/questions "b73355af-8562-58ac-92ab-a09e083ca7d0"] [:db/add "generator" :question-generator/id #uuid "ac3f4ddf-e1ea-578a-85d0-b59d3a1b9f79"] [:db/add "generator" :question-generator/script "generators/4f/4fd06a5b0cf48eeed6d10418e1b6cad209e39ef6a90fedc95a4468179725ac42/generator.py"] [:db/add 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/question-generator "generator"] [:db/ensure 17592186166788 :knowledge-point/validate] [:db/cas 17592186693815 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186693821 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186693830 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694166 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694194 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694197 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694208 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694216 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694227 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694244 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694256 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694258 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694284 :question/retired nil true] [:db/cas 17592186694294 :question/problem "Consider the differential equation

$$

Which of the following are equilibrium solutions? Select all that apply."] [:db/cas 17592186694294 :question/worked-solution "A constant function $y(t)=c$ has derivative $dy/dt=0$. It must satisfy the original equation and its domain restrictions.

The original equation requires $y - 1>0$.

Isolating the derivative gives

$$
\frac{dy}{dt} = y^{2} \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} - 2 y \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + \ln{\left(y - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}.
$$

Test each supplied constant in the original equation, with the derivative set to zero.

- For $y=c=2$, evaluate the non-derivative left and right sides, denoted $L(c)$ and $R(c)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} &= \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\  &= 0 \\ L(c) &= c + 1 \\  &= 3 \\ R(c) &= \left(c + 1\right) + \left(\left(c - 1\right)^{2} \ln{\left(c - 1 \right)} + e^{-2}\right) \\  &= e^{-2} + 3\end{aligned}

$$
f(c) = - 2 c^{2} - 4 c
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1) &=-4 - 2 \\ &=-6\end{aligned}

- For $c=0$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) &=0 + 0 \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(3) &=0\end{aligned}

First keep the original domain: $y + 1>0$.

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
\begin{gathered}f(c)= \\ \left(c - e + 1\right) \ln{\left(c + 1 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

- For $c=1$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(1)= \\ \left(- e + 2\right) \ln{\left(2 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=0$: Use $\ln{\left(1 \right)}=0$.

$$
\begin{gathered}f(0)= \\ \left(- e + 1\right) \ln{\left(1 \right)} \\ =0\end{gathered}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=2$:

$$
\begin{gathered}f(2)= \\ \left(- e + 3\right) \ln{\left(3 \right)}\end{gathered}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-1$, $c + 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

Select $y=0$."] ["9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/hard] ["9d79f37b-975e-5724-99c9-20f14836b61a" :question/answer-fields $$

Test whether $f(c)=0$, where

$$
f(c) = \frac{c^{2} + c - 2}{c - 1}
$$

- For $c=-2$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) &=0\end{aligned}
$$

This is zero, so it is an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=1$, $c - 1=0$ violates the original domain, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=-3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-3) &=-1\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.

- For $c=4$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(4) &=6\end{aligned}
$$

This is nonzero, so it is not an equilibrium solution.
